item.title: Laplace noise has its stated Lebesgue density

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: For every b>0, the probability measure Lap(b) is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on R and has density z↦(2b)⁻¹exp(−|z|/b).
proof_obligations: Derive the positive and reflected negative half-line densities from the exponential density and reflection invariance; handle the singleton {0}.
item.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the exponential-law and Lebesgue-reflection suppliers.

item.title: Laplace mechanism

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: Input a database D, a finite-dimensional query f:D→R^d with finite global L1 sensitivity Δ₁f, and ε>0. If Δ₁f>0, draw Z from the finite product law Lap(Δ₁f/ε)^{⊗d} and release f(D)+Z. If Δ₁f=0, release f(D) deterministically. The output space is R^d with its Borel sigma-algebra.
proof_obligations: Give the exact noise scale, independent-coordinate law, zero-sensitivity branch, and measurable output space; justify the probability-kernel construction from the finite product law.
item.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the real Laplace probability law; the finite product and mechanism construction use no stronger choice principle.

item.title: Differential privacy inequality for bounded measurable functions

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: Let P,Q be probability measures and suppose P(A)≤e^εQ(A)+δ for every measurable A, with ε≥0 and 0≤δ≤1. Then for every measurable g with 0≤g≤1, ∫g dP≤e^ε∫g dQ+δ.
proof_obligations: Approximate g from below by dyadic simple functions, apply the event inequality to each level set, and pass to the limit by monotone convergence.

item.title: Differential privacy is preserved under randomized postprocessing

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: If K is an (ε,δ)-differentially private probability kernel from databases to a measurable output space and L is any data-independent probability kernel from that output space to another measurable space, then the composed kernel KL is (ε,δ)-differentially private.
proof_obligations: For each output event B, apply the bounded-function extension to g(y)=L(y,B), then identify the integrals with the composed-kernel event probabilities.

item.title: Approximate-DP kernels admit a nearby pure-DP kernel on standard-Borel targets

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: Let H and Y be standard-Borel spaces, λ a probability measure on H, and K,L probability kernels H→Y. If for λ-almost every h the pair K(h,·),L(h,·) satisfies both (ε,δ)-DP event inequalities, then there is a probability kernel K* such that for λ-almost every h and every measurable A, e^(−ε)L(h,A)≤K*(h,A)≤e^εL(h,A), and ∫TV(K(h,·),K*(h,·))λ(dh)≤δ, where TV(P,Q)=sup_A|P(A)−Q(A)|.
proof_obligations: Use jointly measurable Radon–Nikodym densities relative to (K+L)/2, clip the density into [e^(−ε)q,e^εq], renormalize within the available slack, prove TV≤δ, and define the kernel measurably on one common conull set.
item.axiom_use: AC is used through the published jointly measurable RN-kernel supplier and the countable measure-determining algebra; no additional choice principle is used.

item.title: Advanced adaptive composition for standard-Borel outputs

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: Assume AC. Let each round output space and every finite transcript-prefix space be standard Borel. For k≥1 adaptive rounds, if each round conditional on every prior transcript is (ε,δ)-differentially private, where ε≥0, 0≤δ≤1, and 0<δ′<1 with kδ+δ′≤1, then the full transcript is (ε′,kδ+δ′)-differentially private, where ε′=√(2k ln(1/δ′))ε+kε(e^ε−1).
proof_obligations: For the pure case, factor the transcript likelihood ratio into conditional RN ratios, bound their conditional KL means and apply Azuma. For approximate DP, purify each round under a base law dominating original and modified transcript prefixes, bound prefix TV cumulatively by kδ, then compose the pure result.
item.axiom_use: Assume full AC for the measurable RN-kernel versions and Azuma supplier. The standard-Borel output assumption is explicit and is the current scope boundary.

item.title: Basic and advanced adaptive composition

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition:
Let databases be finite-support record-count functions, with neighbors differing by one added or removed record occurrence. For $k\ge1$, let round $i$ be a probability kernel $K_i(D,h,\cdot)$ from the $i$th arbitrary measurable output space, conditional on every prior transcript $h$. Suppose that for every ordered neighboring pair $D\sim D'$, every $h$, and every measurable round-$i$ event $A$,
$$
K_i(D,h,A)\le e^{\varepsilon_i}K_i(D',h,A)+\delta_i,
$$
where $\varepsilon_i\ge0$ and $\delta_i\ge0$. If $\sum_i\delta_i\le1$, the full transcript on the finite product sigma-algebra is $(\sum_i\varepsilon_i,\sum_i\delta_i)$-differentially private. Also, assuming AC, if every conditional round has the same parameters $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ with $\varepsilon\ge0$ and $0\le\delta\le1$, then for any $0<\delta'<1$ with $k\delta+\delta'\le1$, advanced composition on arbitrary measurable output spaces gives parameters $(\varepsilon',k\delta+\delta')$, where
$$
\varepsilon'=\sqrt{2k\ln(1/\delta')}\,\varepsilon+k\varepsilon(e^\varepsilon-1).
$$
proof_obligations: Apply the proved arbitrary-output basic and advanced suppliers with their complete hypotheses, declaring AC only for the advanced clause.
item.axiom_use: The basic clause is choice-free. Assume AC for the advanced clause, through the ordinary finite-measure Radon–Nikodym theorem and Azuma supplier; no regular conditional law is used.

item.title: Exponential mechanism privacy and utility

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: Under the exponential-mechanism hypotheses, the output law is (ε,0)-differentially private. For D fixed, let R_OPT={r∈R:u(D,r)=OPTᵤ(D)}. For every t>0, P[u(D,M(D))≤OPTᵤ(D)−(2Δᵤ/ε)(ln(|R|/|R_OPT|)+t)]≤e^(−t).
proof_obligations: Bound both the point-probability and normalizer ratios; for utility, bound bad unnormalized mass and lower-bound the normalizer using all maximizers; verify R_OPT is nonempty.

item.title: Finite-range private selection

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: Let R={a,b} and ε>0. The constant utility u(D,a)=1,u(D,b)=0 has Δᵤ=0 and is inadmissible for the positive-sensitivity exponential mechanism. Fix a record u* and set s(D)=1 exactly when D(u*)>0; define instead u(D,a)=1,u(D,b)=1−s(D). Then Δᵤ=1, the mechanism is (ε,0)-differentially private, and it selects a with probability e^(ε/2)/(e^(ε/2)+e^(ε(1−s(D))/2)).
proof_obligations: Check the first assignment has zero sensitivity and is excluded; for the second, compute Δᵤ=1, normalize both weights, and instantiate the privacy theorem.

item.title: Thresholding a private noisy count

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: Release a Laplace-noised count of records satisfying a fixed predicate, then output 1 exactly when the released real number is at least a fixed threshold c∈R. The threshold decision is a data-independent deterministic postprocessing of the private noisy count and retains the same (ε,0) guarantee.
proof_obligations: Identify the threshold map as a Borel-measurable deterministic kernel independent of the database, then apply the Laplace and postprocessing theorems.
item.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the Laplace noise law.

item.title: Laplace mechanism privacy

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

item.statement_or_definition: For every finite-dimensional query f with finite global L1 sensitivity and every ε>0, the Laplace mechanism is (ε,0)-differentially private under add/remove adjacency.
proof_obligations: Prove the positive-sensitivity density-ratio bound in both directions, integrate over every Borel event, and handle Δ₁f=0 separately.
item.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the real-valued Laplace mechanism; the privacy-ratio argument itself is choice-free.
